body: I followed the same steps mentioned above, but I was unable to reproduce the bug. Since the issue appears to be related to the editor cache, I also tried deleting and rebuilding the `.godot` directory, but the bug still did not occur.

Judging by the functions in the backtrace, it seems related to the resource UI folding behavior (like when you click on arrays or dictionaries or resources to edit, it opens a sub-inspector), so not a `TileSet` issue, I'd say, but maybe a UI cache issue. This is always stored in the `editor` directory of the `.godot` directory. Post the `editor` directory of that here, perhaps, that would help.

I am having this same issue. It seems to be semi resolved when I delete `.godot` but the crash ends up cropping back up when switching between tiles while in setup.

I can provide dump I just dont know where those log to.

Depending on the OS, there'll be a crash handler which if you click on, will give you the backtrace. If there isn't one, though, you should run Godot through the command line like Terminal, then you can see every log of Godot there, including the crash backtrace.

For this specific issue though, the OP already provided a backtrace, so I think it would be helpful if you uploaded the `.godot` folder here, after the crash occurs. Even if there's nothing out of the ordinary there, I would be able to test out fixes for this issue using that folder. As it is, it's not reproducible to test fixes for. It could be the function itself, but I would have to double-check.

I have, unfortunately, seemed to accidentally delete my backed up `.godot` directory which was faulty, and haven't been able to reproduce it since. I'll try again later today, but no promises, as I am not sure what I did to trigger it. 

My only guesstimate (but again, this is just a wild guess for now) would be that it has something to do with parsing the custom tile data layer typing, as I did change the type of one of my layers from an `int` to a `PackedInt32Array` before encountering the crash. It might be possible that the stored fold in the `.godot` cache mismatched the expected type. 

Maybe @drraccoony can help reproduce?

I think I found a path to investigate:

At https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7216a6290065f79d2826d7bd35812add1f513eb8/editor/inspector/editor_properties.cpp#L3794-L3801 `get_edited_object()` might be null, but is left unguarded. 

At https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7216a6290065f79d2826d7bd35812add1f513eb8/modules/tilemap/editor/tile_set_atlas_source_editor.cpp#L628 the edited object is set to a `nullptr`. Then through notification propagation `fold_resource()` might be called while it still expects the edited object to be valid.

Take this with a grain of salt, as I'm not very familiar with the engine code.

I noticed this PR that added that line: #120548, which was merged after `4.7.1.stable` (your tested version). It was merged into `4.7.2.rc1`, which might fix your issue.
